name: New Jersey
note: New Jersey registers every death through the New Jersey Electronic Death Registration System (NJ-EDRS): the funeral director in charge executes the death certificate and files it with the local registrar in exchange for a burial or removal permit, and the attending physician, advanced practice nurse or medical examiner certifies the cause within 24 hours of pronouncement. A record created on NJ-EDRS is deemed transmitted to the State registrar. The statute requires NJ-EDRS, once the record is complete and a burial permit issued, to notify the Social Security Administration, USCIS, the state Medicaid division and the Department of Labor electronically, so registration itself propagates. Municipal officers in charge of death records also file monthly lists with the county commissioner of registration for voter-roll removal, and the State registrar files an annual list.

steps.title: Nurse or PA pronounces death and reports it
steps.who: A registered professional nurse or a physician assistant (physicians also pronounce).
steps.trigger: An apparent death not governed by the brain-death provisions of N.J.S.A. 26:6A-4.
steps.summary: An RN or PA may determine and pronounce death and attests to it by signing the certificate or, for NJ-EDRS, by reporting the pronouncement orally or in writing to the attending, covering or resident physician or the county medical examiner.

steps.title: Notify the medical examiner and county prosecutor
steps.who: The physician in attendance, a law enforcement officer with knowledge, the funeral director, or any other person present.
steps.trigger: Deaths listed in 26:6B-10(a), including criminal violence, accident, suspicious circumstances, suicide, sudden death in apparent good health, death of a child under 18, and death within 24 hours of hospital or nursing-home admission.
steps.summary: Reportable deaths go immediately to the county or intercounty medical examiner and the county prosecutor; the medical examiner takes charge of the body and conducts a medicolegal investigation.

steps.title: Funeral director refers deaths without medical attendance
steps.who: The funeral director (or, if the local registrar is told, the registrar refers the case).
steps.summary: The funeral director notifies the State or county medical examiner (or the local registrar, who refers it on); the medical examiner supplies the cause-of-death particulars or enters them directly into NJ-EDRS.

steps.title: Certify cause of death in NJ-EDRS
steps.who: The attending, covering or resident physician, the attending advanced practice nurse, or the county or intercounty medical examiner.

deadline.text: not to exceed 24 hours after the pronouncement of death

steps.summary: The certifier supplies the death and last-sickness particulars and executes the death certification within 24 hours of pronouncement, authenticating it through NJ-EDRS.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate through NJ-EDRS
steps.who: The funeral director in charge of the funeral or disposition, with personal particulars from the person best qualified to supply them.
steps.trigger: The need for a burial, removal or transit permit.

deadline.text: before burial, removal or other final disposition (no day count in the statute read)

steps.summary: The funeral director is responsible for executing the certificate by means of NJ-EDRS and files it with the local registrar of the district of death (or of the funeral home or place of disposition) in exchange for a burial or removal permit. NJ-EDRS is the required means of registration for every death.

steps.title: Burial or removal permit issued on a complete certificate
steps.trigger: Receipt of a properly executed and complete death certificate.
steps.summary: No body may be buried, otherwise disposed of or removed from the state without a death certificate and a burial or removal permit; the registrar withholds the permit until defects are corrected. In NJ-EDRS the certificate is complete when the certifier and funeral director have completed their portions.

steps.title: NJ-EDRS record deemed transmitted to the State registrar
steps.trigger: Creation of the record on NJ-EDRS.
steps.summary: Paper certificates go to the State registrar by the tenth of each month, but a record created on NJ-EDRS is deemed already transmitted.

steps.title: Certified copies to family, representatives and agencies
steps.who: The State registrar or a local registrar.
steps.trigger: A request with proof of identity and relationship.
steps.summary: Certified copies of a death certificate go to the decedent's parent, guardian or legal representative, spouse or civil union partner, adult child, grandchild or sibling, government agencies for official purposes, holders of a court order, and persons authorised in emergent circumstances. The funeral home recorded on the certificate counts as legal representative.

steps.title: NJ-EDRS notifies the Social Security Administration
steps.who: NJ-EDRS, maintained by the State registrar.
steps.trigger: Completion of the death record and issuance of a burial permit.
steps.latencyNote: upon completion of the death record and issuance of a burial permit (nj-26-8-24.1-b8)
steps.summary: State law requires NJ-EDRS to send the decedent's name, Social Security number, last known address and informant electronically to the federal Social Security Administration.

steps.title: NJ-EDRS notifies the state Medicaid division
steps.who: NJ-EDRS, to the Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services (Department of Human Services).
steps.trigger: Completion of the death record and issuance of a burial permit.
steps.latencyNote: upon completion of the death record and issuance of a burial permit (nj-26-8-24.1-b8)
steps.summary: The same electronic notification goes to the Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services, to safeguard public benefit programs.

steps.title: NJ-EDRS notifies Labor and USCIS
steps.who: NJ-EDRS, to the NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, and other agencies the State registrar designates.
steps.trigger: Completion of the death record and issuance of a burial permit.
steps.latencyNote: upon completion of the death record and issuance of a burial permit (nj-26-8-24.1-b8)
steps.summary: Labor and Workforce Development (unemployment and disability benefits), USCIS and any other agency the State registrar designates also receive the electronic notification, to protect benefit programs and deter identity misuse.

steps.title: Veterans' cremations notified to Veterans Affairs
steps.who: NJ-EDRS, to the Department of Veterans Affairs.
steps.trigger: Completion of the death record and issuance of a cremation permit for a veteran or eligible spouse or dependent.
steps.latencyNote: upon completion of the death record and issuance of the cremation permit (nj-26-8-24.1-b11)
steps.summary: When the record identifies a cremated veteran or eligible spouse or dependent, NJ-EDRS notifies Veterans Affairs with name, address, service dates, date of death and cremation permit date.

steps.title: Monthly list of deceased veterans to county supervisors
steps.who: The State Department of Health, to each county supervisor of veterans' interment.
steps.trigger: Death certificates filed in the preceding month showing burial, cremation or removal in the county.

deadline.text: on or before the tenth day of each month

steps.summary: Each month the Department certifies to the county supervisor of veterans' interment the name of each deceased veteran, with the date and place of disposition and the war served.

steps.title: Municipal death lists to the county commissioner of registration
steps.who: The health officer or other officer in charge of death records in each municipality.
steps.trigger: Deaths of persons aged 18 or over in the municipality.

deadline.text: monthly, in the first five days (every two weeks in the two months before an election)

steps.summary: The municipal officer files the age, date of death, name and address of each adult who died; within 30 days the county commissioner of registration moves matching registrations to the death file. Deaths of residents of another county are forwarded there.

steps.title: State registrar's annual list and voter-system matching
steps.who: The State registrar of vital statistics; the Secretary of State under a matching agreement with the Department of Health.
steps.trigger: Deaths of county residents aged 18 or over in the previous year.

deadline.text: no later than May 1 of each year

steps.summary: The State registrar files an alphabetised list of deceased adult residents with each county commissioner of registration each year, and the statewide voter registration system is matched against Department of Health death records under an agreement the Secretary of State must make.

steps.title: NJ-EDRS notifies the Funeral Directors Association's payment programs
steps.who: NJ-EDRS, to the New Jersey State Funeral Directors Association.
steps.trigger: Death of a participant in one of its funeral expense payment programs.
steps.latencyNote: upon completion of the death record and issuance of a burial permit (nj-26-8-24.1-b8f)
steps.summary: The only private recipient named in the statute: the association is notified so it can meet its fiduciary obligations to pay the decedent's funeral and burial expenses.

steps.title: Informational certifications in other circumstances
steps.who: The State registrar or a local registrar.
steps.trigger: A request from someone who does not qualify for a certified copy.
steps.summary: A certification marked for informational purposes only, not to be used for identification, may be issued in other circumstances. Banks and insurers otherwise rely on the family or the funeral home presenting a certified copy.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: No day count. The statutes set none (the certificate must be filed to obtain the burial or removal permit before disposition; the medical certification is due within 24 hours of pronouncement), and the Department of Health's rules for death records, N.J.A.C. 8:2A (readopted unchanged in 2025), were read in full and set none either: subchapter 3 makes NJ-EDRS the required means of registration and deems the certificate complete when the certifier and funeral director have completed their portions and filed it. The 72-hour filing rule reported elsewhere is not in Title 26 or N.J.A.C. 8:2A.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director in charge executes and files the certificate, obtaining personal particulars from the person best qualified to supply them.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: Medical examiners investigate only the categories of death listed in 26:6B-10; there is no review of every certificate.

electronicRegistration.note: NJ-EDRS is the required means of death registration and certification for every death, subject to case-by-case exceptions approved by the State registrar.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; NJ-EDRS is a vital-records system maintained by the State registrar.

governmentPropagation.note: Completing the NJ-EDRS record and issuing the burial permit triggers statutory electronic notices to SSA, USCIS, state Medicaid and Labor; voter rolls are fed by monthly municipal lists and an annual State registrar list.

certificateAccess.note: Certified copies are restricted to close family, legal representatives (including the funeral home), government agencies and court-order holders; informational certifications may be issued in other circumstances.

privateSectorVerification.note: The only private notification in statute goes to the State Funeral Directors Association's funeral payment programs; others may get informational certifications. No general verification service or duty on banks or insurers was found.

gaps: The 72-hour death-certificate filing rule associated with NJ-EDRS was not found. It is not in Title 26 of the statutes (full-text searches for '72 hours' and 'seventy-two hours' returned nothing relevant), and it is not in N.J.A.C. 8:2A (Death Records): the whole chapter (8:2A-1.1 to 4.2 and its appendix) was read on 28 October 2026 in the Department of Health's compilation at www.nj.gov/health/vital/documents/regulations.pdf, and no section sets a day or hour count for filing. The rule may be in the State Board of Mortuary Science rules (N.J.A.C. 13:36, Division of Consumer Affairs), which were not reached, or may be administrative practice only. registrationDeadlineDays stays null.

No NJ statute was found requiring the Motor Vehicle Commission to cancel a deceased person's licence, or the Division of Taxation to be notified; 19:31-32(e)(1) only matches voter and MVC databases for verification.
N.J.S.A. 26:8-24(i) separately directs the State registrar to facilitate electronic notice to Labor and Human Services; it duplicates 26:8-24.1(b)(8) and was not cited.
Penalties for a funeral director's failure to file (beyond the $25 penalty in 26:6-6(b) for not notifying the State registrar of an out-of-district filing) were not traced in Title 26.

The N.J.A.C. 8:2A text cited here is the Department of Health's own compilation ('NJ Death Regulations'), a scanned PDF with no text layer, so the citation verifier cannot re-read it automatically; quotes were checked by eye. It is undated and still names the 'Department of Health and Senior Services', so it predates 2012. The 2018 and 2025 notices of readoption (nj.gov/health/legal/rules/archive-adoption) readopted the chapter without amendment, but amendments between the compilation and 2018 were not traced. The official N.J.A.C. is published only through LexisNexis, linked from nj.gov/health/legal/rules.
ocsme.nj.gov (Office of the Chief State Medical Examiner) is a client-rendered app with no readable text; it was not used.
